column1: Pour 1 gallon of warm water into a clean bucket or cooler. Add the brown sugar, salt, shallots, garlic, peppercorns, juniper and herbs and stir until the salt and sugar dissolve. Let the brine cool completely.
Lower the turkey into the cold brine and add about 1/2 gallon more cold water, or enough to fully submerge it.
Keep it cold: cover and refrigerate a bucket, or pack a cooler with ice so it stays at 40°F (4°C) or below.
Brine 24–36 hours for a turkey of 15 lb or less, or up to 3 days for a larger bird. For a longer brine on a small turkey cut the salt to 1/2–3/4 cup.
Remove the turkey, drain, and set on a rack. Pat dry and refrigerate uncovered for at least a few hours, ideally overnight, so the skin dries out.
Rub the dry skin all over with softened butter. Optionally tuck herbs into the cavity.
Roast at 325°F (163°C) for about 15 minutes per pound, uncovered at first and tented with foil near the end, until the thickest part of the breast reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest at least 25 minutes before carving.
